Forecasting Monthly Overnight Stays in Portuguese Tourist Accommodation

Revised — adds candidate M7 = SARIMA(1,1,1)(1,1,1)[12] alongside the airline model M1

24 maio 2026

library(rio)
library(forecast)
library(astsa)
library(fpp2)
library(zoo)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(scales)
library(knitr)
library(lubridate)
raw <- import("2MDA08_200002140_202401101_serie_tourism.xlsx")
raw <- raw[order(raw$year, raw$month), ]

original_ts <- ts(raw$Stays, start = c(2006, 1), frequency = 12)

1 Exploratory Data Analysis

1.1 Time plot

autoplot(original_ts / 1000) +
  ggtitle("Monthly overnight stays in tourist accommodation, Portugal") +
  xlab("Year") + ylab("Stays (thousands)") +
  theme_minimal()

Figure 1. Monthly overnight stays in tourist accommodation in Portugal, January 2006 – December 2025 (thousands of stays). Source: INE.

1.2 Seasonal sub-series plot

ggsubseriesplot(original_ts / 1000) +
  ggtitle("Seasonal sub-series plot, Portuguese overnight stays") +
  ylab("Stays (thousands)") + xlab("Month") +
  theme_minimal()

Figure 2. Seasonal sub-series plot of the original series. Each panel shows one calendar month across years; horizontal bars give the within-month means.

1.3 Seasonal overlay plot

ggseasonplot(original_ts / 1000, year.labels = TRUE, year.labels.left = TRUE) +
  ggtitle("Seasonal overlay: stays by month, 2006–2025") +
  ylab("Stays (thousands)") + xlab("Month") +
  theme_minimal()

Figure 3. Seasonal overlay plot, one line per year, 2006–2025.

1.4 Lag plot

gglagplot(original_ts, lags = 12, do.lines = FALSE) +
  ggtitle("Lag plots of monthly stays, lags 1–12") +
  theme_minimal()

Figure 4. Lag plot of the original series, lags 1–12.

1.5 ACF and PACF of the original series

ggtsdisplay(original_ts, lag.max = 48,
            main = "Original series with ACF and PACF (lag.max = 48)",
            theme = theme_minimal())

Figure 5. ACF and PACF of the original series, lags up to 48 months.

1.6 Box-Cox / log transformation

pre_covid <- window(original_ts, end = c(2020, 2))
lambda_pre  <- BoxCox.lambda(pre_covid)
lambda_full <- BoxCox.lambda(original_ts)
par(mfrow = c(2, 1), mar = c(3, 4, 2, 1))
plot(original_ts / 1000, ylab = "Stays (thousands)",
     main = "Original series", col = "steelblue", lwd = 1)
plot(log(original_ts), ylab = "log(Stays)",
     main = "Log-transformed series", col = "steelblue", lwd = 1)

Figure 6. Original series (top) versus log-transformed series (bottom). The log transformation stabilises the seasonal amplitude. 

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

1.7 Implementation

pre_covid_train <- window(original_ts, end = c(2020, 2))

hw_counter <- HoltWinters(pre_covid_train, seasonal = "multiplicative")
hw_counter
## Holt-Winters exponential smoothing with trend and multiplicative seasonal component.
## 
## Call:
## HoltWinters(x = pre_covid_train, seasonal = "multiplicative")
## 
## Smoothing parameters:
##  alpha: 0.2263
##  beta : 0
##  gamma: 0.7443
## 
## Coefficients:
##             [,1]
## a   6253221.4034
## b     17494.3325
## s1        0.7918
## s2        1.0017
## s3        1.1100
## s4        1.2083
## s5        1.4003
## s6        1.6382
## s7        1.2972
## s8        1.0876
## s9        0.6736
## s10       0.5730
## s11       0.5267
## s12       0.6028
covid_steps <- 34
hw_pred     <- forecast(hw_counter, h = covid_steps, level = 95)

covid_window <- window(original_ts, start = c(2020, 3), end = c(2022, 12))
counter_vals <- as.numeric(hw_pred$mean)

adjusted_vec <- as.numeric(original_ts)
covid_idx <- seq(which(time(original_ts) == 2020 + 2/12),
                 by = 1, length.out = covid_steps)
adjusted_vec[covid_idx] <- counter_vals
adjusted_ts <- ts(adjusted_vec, start = c(2006, 1), frequency = 12)
plot(adjusted_ts / 1000, col = "firebrick", lwd = 1.2,
     ylab = "Stays (thousands)", xlab = "Year",
     main = "Original vs COVID-adjusted series")
lines(original_ts / 1000, col = "steelblue", lwd = 1.2)
abline(v = c(2020 + 2/12, 2023), lty = 2, col = "grey40")
legend("topleft", legend = c("Original", "Adjusted (counterfactual)"),
       col = c("steelblue", "firebrick"), lwd = 1.2, bty = "n")

Figure 7. Original series (blue) and COVID-adjusted counterfactual series (red). Vertical dashed lines mark the disrupted window (March 2020 – December 2022). 

plot(window(adjusted_ts / 1000, start = c(2018, 1), end = c(2024, 12)),
     col = "firebrick", lwd = 1.3,
     ylab = "Stays (thousands)", xlab = "Year",
     main = "Zoom on 2018–2024: counterfactual replacement of COVID period")
lines(window(original_ts / 1000, start = c(2018, 1), end = c(2024, 12)),
      col = "steelblue", lwd = 1.3)
abline(v = c(2020 + 2/12, 2023), lty = 2, col = "grey40")
legend("topleft", legend = c("Original", "Adjusted"),
       col = c("steelblue", "firebrick"), lwd = 1.3, bty = "n")

Figure 8. Zoom on the COVID window. The red curve is the HW counterfactual that replaces the observed values during the disruption. 

lambda_adj <- BoxCox.lambda(adjusted_ts)

2 Smoothing and decomposition methods

2.1 STL decomposition on the full adjusted series

stl_full <- stl(adjusted_ts, s.window = "periodic",
                robust = TRUE, inner = 2, outer = 19)
plot(stl_full, main = "STL decomposition of adjusted stays (s.window = periodic, robust)")

Figure 9. STL decomposition of the adjusted series: data, seasonal, trend-cycle and remainder components.

2.1.1 Components in detail

trend_c    <- stl_full$time.series[, "trend"]
seasonal_c <- stl_full$time.series[, "seasonal"]
remainder  <- stl_full$time.series[, "remainder"]

autoplot(trend_c / 1000) +
  ggtitle("Trend-cycle component") +
  xlab("Year") + ylab("Stays (thousands)") + theme_minimal()

Figure 10. Trend-cycle component extracted by STL.

.

autoplot(seasonal_c / 1000) +
  ggtitle("Seasonal component (periodic)") +
  xlab("Year") + ylab("Deviation from trend (thousands)") + theme_minimal()

Figure 11. Seasonal component extracted by STL (forced periodic). 

autoplot(remainder / 1000) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  ggtitle("Remainder component") +
  xlab("Year") + ylab("Stays (thousands)") + theme_minimal()

Figure 12. Remainder component, with horizontal reference at zero.

.

ggtsdisplay(remainder, lag.max = 48,
            main = "ACF and PACF of the STL remainder",
            theme = theme_minimal())

Figure 13. ACF and PACF of the STL remainder, lags up to 48.

2.1.2 Seasonally adjusted series

seasadj_ts <- adjusted_ts - seasonal_c

autoplot(adjusted_ts / 1000, series = "Adjusted series") +
  autolayer(seasadj_ts / 1000, series = "Seasonally adjusted") +
  ggtitle("Adjusted vs seasonally adjusted stays") +
  xlab("Year") + ylab("Stays (thousands)") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Adjusted series" = "steelblue",
                                 "Seasonally adjusted" = "firebrick")) +
  theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "bottom")

Figure 14. Original (adjusted) series vs seasonally adjusted series. Removing the seasonal component reveals the underlying trend-cycle.

2.2 Holt-Winters exponential smoothing

train_ts <- window(adjusted_ts, end   = c(2024, 12))
test_ts  <- window(adjusted_ts, start = c(2025,  1))
c(train_n = length(train_ts), test_n = length(test_ts))
## train_n  test_n 
##     228      12

2.2.1 Multiplicative Holt-Winters

hw_mult <- HoltWinters(train_ts, seasonal = "multiplicative")
hw_mult
## Holt-Winters exponential smoothing with trend and multiplicative seasonal component.
## 
## Call:
## HoltWinters(x = train_ts, seasonal = "multiplicative")
## 
## Smoothing parameters:
##  alpha: 0.7498
##  beta : 0
##  gamma: 0.5472
## 
## Coefficients:
##             [,1]
## a   7652102.8074
## b     17494.3325
## s1        0.5031
## s2        0.6081
## s3        0.8202
## s4        1.0399
## s5        1.1665
## s6        1.2347
## s7        1.4364
## s8        1.6792
## s9        1.3242
## s10       1.0960
## s11       0.6476
## s12       0.5427
hw_mult_coefs <- coef(hw_mult)
hw_mult_coefs[grep("^s", names(hw_mult_coefs))]
##     s1     s2     s3     s4     s5     s6     s7     s8     s9    s10    s11 
## 0.5031 0.6081 0.8202 1.0399 1.1665 1.2347 1.4364 1.6792 1.3242 1.0960 0.6476 
##    s12 
## 0.5427

2.2.3 Forecasts on the test set

fc_hw_mult <- forecast(hw_mult, h = 12, level = 95)
fc_hw_add  <- forecast(hw_add,  h = 12, level = 95)
autoplot(fc_hw_mult, include = 84) +
  autolayer(test_ts, series = "Observed 2025", colour = TRUE) +
  ggtitle("Multiplicative Holt-Winters forecast for 2025") +
  xlab("Year") + ylab("Stays") +
  theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "bottom")

Figure 15. Multiplicative Holt-Winters forecast (blue) and 95% PI shaded, for January – December 2025, overlaid on the observed (adjusted) series. Black points show the realised 2025 values. 

acc_hw_mult <- accuracy(fc_hw_mult, test_ts)
acc_hw_add  <- accuracy(fc_hw_add,  test_ts)

acc_hw_table <- rbind(
  "HW multiplicative (train)" = acc_hw_mult["Training set", c("RMSE", "MAE", "MAPE")],
  "HW multiplicative (test)"  = acc_hw_mult["Test set",     c("RMSE", "MAE", "MAPE")],
  "HW additive (train)"       = acc_hw_add[ "Training set", c("RMSE", "MAE", "MAPE")],
  "HW additive (test)"        = acc_hw_add[ "Test set",     c("RMSE", "MAE", "MAPE")]
)
kable(acc_hw_table, digits = 1,
      caption = "Table 1. Accuracy of Holt-Winters models on the 2025 test set.")
Table 1. Accuracy of Holt-Winters models on the 2025 test set.
RMSE MAE MAPE
HW multiplicative (train) 231480 174035 4.2
HW multiplicative (test) 1234838 995349 12.7
HW additive (train) 235320 177290 4.5
HW additive (test) 218284 177328 2.7

2.3 Forecasts from the STL decomposition

fc_stl <- stlf(train_ts,
               s.window = "periodic", robust = TRUE,
               method   = "ets",
               etsmodel = "AAN",
               lambda   = 0,           # work in log space, back-transform automatically
               biasadj  = TRUE,        # mean-unbiased back-transform
               h = 12, level = 95)
autoplot(fc_stl, include = 84) +
  autolayer(test_ts, series = "Observed 2025", colour = TRUE) +
  ggtitle("STL + ETS(A,A,N) forecast for 2025 (log + biasadj)") +
  xlab("Year") + ylab("Stays") +
  theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "bottom")

Figure 15b. STL+ETS forecast (red) and 95% PI for January – December 2025, overlaid on the observed (adjusted) series (black). 

acc_stl <- accuracy(fc_stl, test_ts)
kable(acc_stl[, c("RMSE", "MAE", "MAPE")], digits = 1,
      caption = "Table 1b. Accuracy of the STL + ETS forecast on the 2025 test set.")

RMSE MAE MAPE
Training set 207967 154942 3.5

3 SARIMA modelling and forecasting

log_train <- log(train_ts)
log_test  <- log(test_ts)

3.1 Transformation: the log

ggtsdisplay(log_train, lag.max = 48,
            main = "Log training series with ACF and PACF",
            theme = theme_minimal())

Figure 16. Log-transformed training series with ACF and PACF (lag.max = 48).

3.2 Differencing

D_seas <- nsdiffs(log_train)
d_reg  <- ndiffs(diff(log_train, 12), alpha = 0.05, test = "adf")
d_chk  <- ndiffs(diff(diff(log_train, 12), 1), alpha = 0.05, test = "adf")
c(D = D_seas, d = d_reg, verification = d_chk)
##            D            d verification 
##            1            0            0
stationary <- diff(diff(log_train, 12), 1)
ggtsdisplay(stationary, lag.max = 48,
            main = "Stationary series (∇∇₁₂ log y) with ACF and PACF",
            theme = theme_minimal())

Figure 17. Stationary series (one regular and one seasonal difference of the log training data) with ACF and PACF.

3.3 Model identification from ACF and PACF

Model Specification Motivation from ACF/PACF
M1 \(\text{SARIMA}(0,1,1)\times(0,1,1)_{12}\) “Airline” model — ACF spikes at lags 1 and 12.
M2 \(\text{SARIMA}(1,1,0)\times(1,1,0)_{12}\) PACF interpretation: AR(1) + seasonal AR(1).
M3 \(\text{SARIMA}(1,1,1)\times(0,1,1)\_{12}\) Mixed non-seasonal + seasonal MA(1).
M4 \(\text{SARIMA}(0,1,1)\times(1,1,0)_{12}\) Non-seasonal MA(1) + seasonal AR(1).
M5 \(\text{SARIMA}(1,1,0)\times(0,1,1)_{12}\) Non-seasonal AR(1) + seasonal MA(1).
M6 \(\text{SARIMA}(2,1,1)\times(0,1,1)_{12}\) Extended non-seasonal block.
M7 \(\text{SARIMA}(1,1,1)\times(1,1,1)_{12}\) Airline + AR(1) on both non-seasonal and seasonal sides — addresses residual autocorrelation left by M1.

For comparison we also fit auto.arima as a benchmark.

3.4 Estimation and diagnostics

3.4.1 M1 — SARIMA(0,1,1)(0,1,1)[12] — the “airline” model

M1.fit <- sarima(log_train, p = 0, d = 1, q = 1, P = 0, D = 1, Q = 1, S = 12)

## iter   2 value -3.066883

3.4.7 M7 — SARIMA(1,1,1)(1,1,1)[12]

Following the diagnostic finding that M1 leaves some residual autocorrelation at low lags and around the seasonal lag, we add a non-seasonal AR(1) and a seasonal AR(1) on top of the airline structure.

## ar1   -0.1534 0.1501  -1.022  0.3078
## ma1   -0.3768 0.1480  -2.546  0.0116
## sar1  -0.1709 0.1308  -1.306  0.1928
## sma1  -0.3476 0.1305  -2.663  0.0083
## 
## sigma^2 estimated as 0.002103 on 211 degrees of freedom 
##  
## AIC = -3.263  AICc = -3.263  BIC = -3.185 
##

The coefficient table allows two key sanity checks: (i) whether the new AR terms are individually significant, and (ii) whether AR/MA near-cancellation occurs on either side (i.e. \(\hat\phi_1 \approx -\hat\theta_1\) or \(\hat\Phi_1 \approx -\hat\Theta_1\)), which would suggest the extra parameters are not doing useful work.

M7.fit$ttable
## NULL

We refit M7 the same way, so the forecasting strategies below can be applied to both models with identical machinery.

3.5.1 Residual diagnostic comparison: M1 vs M7

The motivation for testing M7 is residual autocorrelation, not information criteria. We therefore compare ACF/PACF of the in-sample residuals directly.

par(mfrow = c(2, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1))
acf(residuals(M1.arima),  lag.max = 48, main = "M1 residuals — ACF")
pacf(residuals(M1.arima), lag.max = 48, main = "M1 residuals — PACF")
acf(residuals(M7.arima),  lag.max = 48, main = "M7 residuals — ACF")
pacf(residuals(M7.arima), lag.max = 48, main = "M7 residuals — PACF")

Figure 17b. Residual ACF and PACF for M1 (top two panels) and M7 (bottom two panels), lags up to 48. The relevant question is whether M7 brings the spikes inside the bounds at the lags where M1 leaves structure. 

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
lb_lags <- c(6, 12, 18, 24, 36)
lb_M1 <- sapply(lb_lags, function(L)
  Box.test(residuals(M1.arima), lag = L, type = "Ljung-Box",
           fitdf = length(M1.arima$coef))$p.value)
lb_M7 <- sapply(lb_lags, function(L)
  Box.test(residuals(M7.arima), lag = L, type = "Ljung-Box",
           fitdf = length(M7.arima$coef))$p.value)
lb_tab <- data.frame(Lag = lb_lags,
                     `M1 p-value` = round(lb_M1, 4),
                     `M7 p-value` = round(lb_M7, 4),
                     check.names = FALSE)
kable(lb_tab,
      caption = "Table 2b. Ljung-Box test p-values on residuals at selected lags. Larger p-values (> 0.05) are consistent with white-noise residuals.")

3.6 Forecasting strategies

ts_to_df <- function(x) {
  data.frame(
    time  = as.Date(as.yearmon(time(x))),
    value = as.numeric(x)
  )
}
df_to_ts <- function(df) {
  ts(df$value, frequency = 12,
     start = c(year(df$time[1]), month(df$time[1])))
}

adj_df <- ts_to_df(adjusted_ts)

3.6.1 Strategy 1 — fixed training, 12-step ahead

# M1
fc_S1 <- forecast(M1.arima, h = 12, level = 95)
S1_mean_log  <- fc_S1$mean
S1_mean_orig <- exp(S1_mean_log)
S1_lo_orig   <- exp(fc_S1$lower[, 1])
S1_hi_orig   <- exp(fc_S1$upper[, 1])

# M7
fc_S1_M7 <- forecast(M7.arima, h = 12, level = 95)
S1_M7_mean_log  <- fc_S1_M7$mean
S1_M7_mean_orig <- exp(S1_M7_mean_log)
S1_M7_lo_orig   <- exp(fc_S1_M7$lower[, 1])
S1_M7_hi_orig   <- exp(fc_S1_M7$upper[, 1])

One model is estimated on the full training data and used to forecast all 12 months ahead. Forecast uncertainty grows with horizon. Both M1 and M7 are evaluated.

3.6.2 Strategy 2 — fixed model, 1-step interaction

# M1
out <- data.frame()
for (i in 1:12) {
  sub <- adj_df %>%
    filter(time <= as.Date("2024-12-01") %m+% months(i))
  ts_sel <- ts(log(sub$value), frequency = 12,
               end = c(year(tail(sub$time, 1)),
                       month(tail(sub$time, 1))))
  fit <- Arima(ts_sel, model = M1.arima)
  out <- bind_rows(out, data.frame(
    time  = as.Date("2024-12-01") %m+% months(i),
    value = tail(fitted(fit), 1)
  ))
}
S2_mean_log  <- df_to_ts(out)
S2_mean_orig <- exp(S2_mean_log)

# M7
out <- data.frame()
for (i in 1:12) {
  sub <- adj_df %>%
    filter(time <= as.Date("2024-12-01") %m+% months(i))
  ts_sel <- ts(log(sub$value), frequency = 12,
               end = c(year(tail(sub$time, 1)),
                       month(tail(sub$time, 1))))
  fit <- Arima(ts_sel, model = M7.arima)
  out <- bind_rows(out, data.frame(
    time  = as.Date("2024-12-01") %m+% months(i),
    value = tail(fitted(fit), 1)
  ))
}
S2_M7_mean_log  <- df_to_ts(out)
S2_M7_mean_orig <- exp(S2_M7_mean_log)

The estimated model is not re-estimated; instead, at each step the training data are extended by one observation and the model is applied (parameters fixed) to produce a one-step-ahead fitted value. This tests how each fixed model adapts.

3.6.3 Strategy 3 — expanding windows, 1-step ahead

# M1
out <- data.frame()
for (i in 0:11) {
  sub <- adj_df %>%
    filter(time <= as.Date("2024-12-01") %m+% months(i))
  ts_sel <- ts(log(sub$value), frequency = 12,
               end = c(year(tail(sub$time, 1)),
                       month(tail(sub$time, 1))))
  fit <- Arima(ts_sel, order = c(0, 1, 1), seasonal = c(0, 1, 1))
  fct <- forecast(fit, h = 1, level = 95)
  out <- bind_rows(out, data.frame(
    time  = as.Date("2025-01-01") %m+% months(i),
    value = as.numeric(fct$mean),
    lo    = as.numeric(fct$lower[, 1]),
    hi    = as.numeric(fct$upper[, 1])
  ))
}
S3_mean_log  <- df_to_ts(out[, c("time", "value")])
S3_mean_orig <- exp(S3_mean_log)
S3_lo_orig   <- exp(df_to_ts(data.frame(time = out$time, value = out$lo)))
S3_hi_orig   <- exp(df_to_ts(data.frame(time = out$time, value = out$hi)))

# M7
out <- data.frame()
for (i in 0:11) {
  sub <- adj_df %>%
    filter(time <= as.Date("2024-12-01") %m+% months(i))
  ts_sel <- ts(log(sub$value), frequency = 12,
               end = c(year(tail(sub$time, 1)),
                       month(tail(sub$time, 1))))
  fit <- Arima(ts_sel, order = c(1, 1, 1), seasonal = c(1, 1, 1))
  fct <- forecast(fit, h = 1, level = 95)
  out <- bind_rows(out, data.frame(
    time  = as.Date("2025-01-01") %m+% months(i),
    value = as.numeric(fct$mean),
    lo    = as.numeric(fct$lower[, 1]),
    hi    = as.numeric(fct$upper[, 1])
  ))
}
S3_M7_mean_log  <- df_to_ts(out[, c("time", "value")])
S3_M7_mean_orig <- exp(S3_M7_mean_log)
S3_M7_lo_orig   <- exp(df_to_ts(data.frame(time = out$time, value = out$lo)))
S3_M7_hi_orig   <- exp(df_to_ts(data.frame(time = out$time, value = out$hi)))

At each step the model is re-estimated on a growing training sample and then used to produce a one-step-ahead forecast. This is the strategy that should give the best one-step-ahead accuracy if the specification is correct.

3.6.4 Strategy 4 — recursive (sliding) windows, 1-step ahead

# M1
out <- data.frame()
for (i in 0:11) {
  sub <- adj_df %>%
    filter(time >= as.Date("2006-01-01") %m+% months(i) &
           time <= as.Date("2024-12-01") %m+% months(i))
  ts_sel <- ts(log(sub$value), frequency = 12,
               end = c(year(tail(sub$time, 1)),
                       month(tail(sub$time, 1))))
  fit <- Arima(ts_sel, order = c(0, 1, 1), seasonal = c(0, 1, 1))
  fct <- forecast(fit, h = 1, level = 95)
  out <- bind_rows(out, data.frame(
    time  = as.Date("2025-01-01") %m+% months(i),
    value = as.numeric(fct$mean)
  ))
}
S4_mean_log  <- df_to_ts(out)
S4_mean_orig <- exp(S4_mean_log)

# M7
out <- data.frame()
for (i in 0:11) {
  sub <- adj_df %>%
    filter(time >= as.Date("2006-01-01") %m+% months(i) &
           time <= as.Date("2024-12-01") %m+% months(i))
  ts_sel <- ts(log(sub$value), frequency = 12,
               end = c(year(tail(sub$time, 1)),
                       month(tail(sub$time, 1))))
  fit <- Arima(ts_sel, order = c(1, 1, 1), seasonal = c(1, 1, 1))
  fct <- forecast(fit, h = 1, level = 95)
  out <- bind_rows(out, data.frame(
    time  = as.Date("2025-01-01") %m+% months(i),
    value = as.numeric(fct$mean)
  ))
}
S4_M7_mean_log  <- df_to_ts(out)
S4_M7_mean_orig <- exp(S4_M7_mean_log)

The window size is fixed (228 observations) and slides forward by one observation at each step. This protects the parameter estimates against the influence of old data.

As expected, the one-step strategies (S2–S4) are substantially more accurate than the 12-step strategy (S1) for both models. The relevant comparison for the M1-vs-M7 decision is row-by-row within each strategy: if M7 systematically reduces RMSE/MAE/MAPE, the extra parameters are earning their keep; if differences are negligible, the airline model M1 should be preferred on parsimony grounds.

4.2 Month-by-month comparison and 95 % PI coverage

# M1
m1_aux <- sarima.for(log_train, n.ahead = 12,
                     p = 0, d = 1, q = 1, P = 0, D = 1, Q = 1, S = 12,
                     plot = FALSE)
sarima_pt_orig <- exp(m1_aux$pred)
sarima_lo_orig <- exp(m1_aux$pred - 1.96 * m1_aux$se)
sarima_hi_orig <- exp(m1_aux$pred + 1.96 * m1_aux$se)

# M7
m7_aux <- sarima.for(log_train, n.ahead = 12,
                     p = 1, d = 1, q = 1, P = 1, D = 1, Q = 1, S = 12,
                     plot = FALSE)
sarima_m7_pt_orig <- exp(m7_aux$pred)
sarima_m7_lo_orig <- exp(m7_aux$pred - 1.96 * m7_aux$se)
sarima_m7_hi_orig <- exp(m7_aux$pred + 1.96 * m7_aux$se)

monthly_tab <- data.frame(
  Month       = format(as.yearmon(time(test_ts))),
  Observed    = round(as.numeric(test_ts), 0),
  HW_forecast = round(as.numeric(fc_hw_mult$mean), 0),
  HW_PE_pct   = percent(as.numeric((test_ts - fc_hw_mult$mean) / test_ts), accuracy = 0.1),
  HW_in_PI    = between(as.numeric(test_ts),
                        as.numeric(fc_hw_mult$lower[, 1]),
                        as.numeric(fc_hw_mult$upper[, 1])),
  M1_forecast = round(as.numeric(sarima_pt_orig), 0),
  M1_PE_pct   = percent(as.numeric((test_ts - sarima_pt_orig) / test_ts), accuracy = 0.1),
  M1_in_PI    = between(as.numeric(test_ts),
                        as.numeric(sarima_lo_orig),
                        as.numeric(sarima_hi_orig)),
  M7_forecast = round(as.numeric(sarima_m7_pt_orig), 0),
  M7_PE_pct   = percent(as.numeric((test_ts - sarima_m7_pt_orig) / test_ts), accuracy = 0.1),
  M7_in_PI    = between(as.numeric(test_ts),
                        as.numeric(sarima_m7_lo_orig),
                        as.numeric(sarima_m7_hi_orig))
)

Figure 20. 2025 observed (black) vs SARIMA M1 12-step (red), SARIMA M7 12-step (orange), and HW multiplicative 12-step (blue) point forecasts, with 95% PIs (dashed).

4.4 Which method gives the better forecasts?

The SARIMA M1 (2.4 % MAPE on the 12-step strategy) beats the 12-step Holt-Winters forecast (around 12.7 % MAPE), and the one-step SARIMA strategies bring MAPE down further to around 2 %.

The SARIMA M7 specification — recommended on the basis of residual diagnostics rather than information criteria — achieves 2.2 % MAPE on the 12-step strategy and a minimum of 1.7 % across its one-step strategies. The verdict between M1 and M7 should combine (i) residual adequacy (Table 2b), (ii) information criteria (Table 2), and (iii) test-set accuracy (Tables 3–4); if M7 cleans the residual ACF but matches M1 on accuracy, both models are defensible and the choice is a parsimony-vs-adequacy trade-off.

5 Out-of-sample forecasts for 2026

5.1 Re-fitting the models

hw_full <- HoltWinters(adjusted_ts, seasonal = "multiplicative")

fc_stl_full <- stlf(adjusted_ts, s.window = "periodic", robust = TRUE,
                    method = "ets", etsmodel = "AAN",
                    lambda = 0, biasadj = TRUE,
                    h = 12, level = 95)

m1_full_log <- Arima(log(adjusted_ts), order = c(0, 1, 1), seasonal = c(0, 1, 1))
m1_full_log
## Series: log(adjusted_ts) 
## ARIMA(0,1,1)(0,1,1)[12] 
## 
## Coefficients:
##          ma1    sma1
##       -0.513  -0.489
## s.e.   0.068   0.063
## 
## sigma^2 = 0.00208:  log likelihood = 378.9
## AIC=-751.9   AICc=-751.8   BIC=-741.6
m7_full_log <- Arima(log(adjusted_ts), order = c(1, 1, 1), seasonal = c(1, 1, 1))
m7_full_log
## Series: log(adjusted_ts) 
## ARIMA(1,1,1)(1,1,1)[12] 
## 
## Coefficients:
##          ar1     ma1    sar1    sma1
##       -0.131  -0.396  -0.197  -0.331
## s.e.   0.154   0.151   0.123   0.123
## 
## sigma^2 = 0.00207:  log likelihood = 380.4
## AIC=-750.7   AICc=-750.5   BIC=-733.6

5.2 Forecasting January – December 2026

fc_hw_2026 <- forecast(hw_full, h = 12, level = 95)

fc_sarima_2026_log <- forecast(m1_full_log, h = 12, level = 95)
fc_sarima_pt  <- exp(fc_sarima_2026_log$mean)
fc_sarima_lo  <- exp(fc_sarima_2026_log$lower[, 1])
fc_sarima_hi  <- exp(fc_sarima_2026_log$upper[, 1])

fc_sarima_m7_2026_log <- forecast(m7_full_log, h = 12, level = 95)
fc_sarima_m7_pt <- exp(fc_sarima_m7_2026_log$mean)
fc_sarima_m7_lo <- exp(fc_sarima_m7_2026_log$lower[, 1])
fc_sarima_m7_hi <- exp(fc_sarima_m7_2026_log$upper[, 1])

  STL_hi95      = round(as.numeric(fc_stl_full$upper[, 1]), 0),

  M1_lo95       = round(as.numeric(fc_sarima_lo), 0),
  M1_hi95       = round(as.numeric(fc_sarima_hi), 0),

)
